doc: SPORE design tokens — HARDBRUT (supernihil/hardbrut v0.6). See docs/VISUALDESIGN.md §1.
note: The one place a colour is defined. docs/VISUALDESIGN.md stays normative for the *reasoning*; this file is normative for the *values*, and design/generate.py emits them into site/style.css, web/build-standalone.mjs, android Chrome.kt and VISUALDESIGN's contrast table. Contrast ratios are computed from these hexes, never typed. Changing a value here and regenerating is the whole workflow; CI fails if the tree is stale. HARDBRUT is light-first: cream paper, black ink, yellow actions, zero radius, hard no-blur shadows. Two button kinds — default (yellow) and cancel (white). Auto dark mode plus a manual toggle.

dark.doc: The dark side of HARDBRUT. Same shape, inverted ink/paper; the yellow accent is the one colour that does not change between themes, so text sitting on yellow is set in a near-black (OnYellow) rather than the near-white ink.

palette.label: Ink
palette.role: text, borders, chrome in dark mode

palette.label: Paper
palette.role: panels, cards, raised surfaces in dark mode

palette.label: Yellow
palette.role: primary actions, highlights — the one colour shared by both themes

palette.label: On Yellow
palette.role: text sitting on the yellow face in dark mode — near-black, not the near-white ink

semantic.role: success, verified, delivered — always paired with a check, never colour alone
failure — signalled by icon and words, never colour alone

light.doc: Hardbrut light — the default. Cream paper, black ink.

semantic.role: success, verified, delivered — always paired with a check, never colour alone
failure — signalled by icon and words, never colour alone

fonts.stack: ui-monospace, "Cascadia Code", "Fira Code", Menlo, Consolas, monospace
Impact, "Arial Narrow Bold", Haettenschweiler, system-ui, sans-serif
fonts.note: No webfont: the standalone node must make zero network requests, and CI asserts it. A display face is a system stack or it is nothing.

contrast.note: HARDBRUT is measured, not eyeballed. Grades are asserted both ways: a pair declared readable must compute readable, and a pair declared forbidden must compute forbidden. The light theme is the default and is asserted hard; the dark theme is asserted where its tokens differ. Yellow-on-cream is the one forbidden pair the palette invites.
prose_notes:
**Never put yellow on cream.** {yellow_on_bg}:1 — the one combination the palette
invites, and the one nobody can read. Yellow always sits on black ink or owns
its own solid block, never on the paper base.

**Never signal failure by colour alone.** HARDBRUT has no red; failure is an
icon plus words, always.
contrast.prose_notes_doc: Authored prose, computed numbers. The wording is human — 'cream' reads better than the token name — but every ratio in it is substituted from the hexes, so the sentences cannot outlive the palette they describe.

metrics.doc: Sizing, spacing and shape. HARDBRUT: zero border-radius (unless a shape demands it — radios are circles), hard no-blur shadows, 3px borders, and spacing on a 12/24/40 rhythm.
metrics.note: Every value here is one already in the tree, lifted rather than invented. The HARDBRUT adaptation guide names the three sizes and the spacing rhythm explicitly.
metrics.units: dp on Android, px on the web. The two agree by construction at 1x.

controls.role: primary and secondary buttons, and text fields — one height for all three
compact presets and toggles (offline-window, topics). Must still carry a 48dp touch target
list rows — the unit the Bridges/Advanced restructure is built from

shape.role: corner radius — zero. Always. True circles (radio, avatar) are the only exception

touch.role: WCAG/Material floor. control and row clear it by height; chip must be padded out to it.

site.note: The docs site. Light-first (cream paper); dark mode via prefers-color-scheme. HARDBRUT needs no --prose: black ink on cream is already the most readable pairing.

standalone.note: One self-contained file, so it inlines resolved hexes for every colour the components use, plus the mono+display font stacks.

android.note: Compose reads raw colours and maps them in SporeDarkColors/SporeLightColors. Light members are suffixless (Ink/Paper/Yellow/Muted/Bg); dark members carry a Dark suffix, so both themes live in one object without name collisions.
